newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mixed, USG again gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mixed, USG again gains.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed Tuesday in thin trade, with East Coast mostly holding, while the Gulf Coast still seemed well supported by recent Florida demand and some high sulphur interest for Mexico.

"The East Coast is taking a rest because the hot weather has abated and gas is a little sloppy, but Florida is smoking. There's probably a little more supply than demand in the East, while the Gulf looks a little short," said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held relatively steady at about $17 a barrel, with August paper done at $16.55, up 15 cents on firmer crude, traders said.
New York high sulphurs mostly held steady, with 2.2 percent still talked in the low-$15s.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour slipped a quarter to $18.00-25 amid prospects for more nuclear power supply.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent climbed 25 cents to the low-$16s, helped by forecasts for more heat in Florida and expectations a utility there would tender Wednesday for 200,000 barrels of one percent and a small quantity of diesel. The tender announcement had been expected today.
USG three percent also gained slightly to about the $14 level, with buying interest for Mexico still supporting the grade.

New York city gate swing gas prices stayed unchanged Tuesday in the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $15.00 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also held steady at about $2.13/mmBtu, or $13.42 a barrel.
